dispute.riderClaim: I was charged a no-show fee but I was only a few minutes late. The driver cancelled on me.
dispute.driverStatement: I arrived at the pickup, messaged and called the rider, and waited more than five minutes before cancelling.

cases.summary: The driver's no-show cancellation is fully supported by the current-trip evidence. GPS shows the driver came within 31 m of the pickup (limit 150 m), waited 430 s from first entering the threshold until cancelling (minimum 300 s), and the chat/call log shows three contact attempts before cancellation (minimum 1). All three NS-1 conditions are met, so the no-show fee should be retained.

arguments.claim: The driver came within 150 m of the pickup point: closest approach was 31 m, well inside the NS-1 limit.
The driver waited at least 300 seconds before cancelling: 430 s elapsed from first coming within 150 m (09:42:44Z) to cancellation (09:49:54Z).
The driver made at least one recorded contact attempt before cancelling: three attempts (CHAT-01, CHAT-03, CALL-01), exceeding the NS-1 minimum of one.
The rider acknowledged the driver's arrival and said they were coming in 2 minutes, but did not appear within the remaining wait window.
The no-show fee charged (S$5.00) matches the rate card and the payment arithmetic is valid, so the retained amount is correct.

counterevidence.claim: The rider claims they were only a few minutes late, which could suggest the wait was not excessive; however, the recorded wait of 430 s already exceeds the 300 s policy minimum, so lateness beyond the threshold does not defeat the no-show conditions.

The driver's history shows a 3.9 rating and 6 disputes against in 90 days, which could raise credibility concerns, but NS-4 makes history context only and it cannot override the current-trip evidence.

missingFacts: Whether the rider attempted to contact the driver or arrived at the pickup after the cancellation.
The rider's precise location during the wait window, to corroborate the 'few minutes late' claim.
Whether the driver's marked-arrival location matched the designated pickup pin beyond the 31 m closest approach.

cases.summary: The rider was charged a S$5.00 no-show fee after the driver cancelled. The rider claims they were only a few minutes late and the driver cancelled on them. However, the retrieved GPS and chat evidence shows all three NS-1 conditions were satisfied: the driver came within 31 m of the pickup (limit 150 m), waited 430 s from first coming within 150 m until cancelling (minimum 300 s), and made three recorded contact attempts (CHAT-01, CHAT-03, CALL-01) before cancelling. Under NS-1 the fee is properly retained, and NS-2's refund trigger is not met. The rider's own message CHAT-02 ('Ok, coming in 2 minutes.') corroborates that the rider was still en route while the driver waited. The rider's position is therefore not supported by the evidence, and the appropriate remedy is to keep the charge.

arguments.claim: The driver satisfied the distance condition: closest approach to the pickup was 31 m, well within the 150 m limit.
The driver satisfied the waiting condition: 430 seconds elapsed from first coming within 150 m until cancellation, exceeding the 300-second minimum.
The driver satisfied the contact condition: three contact attempts were recorded before cancellation (CHAT-01, CHAT-03, CALL-01), exceeding the minimum of one.
Because all three NS-1 conditions are met, the no-show fee is properly retained and NS-2's refund trigger is not engaged.

counterevidence.claim: The rider's account of being only a few minutes late is partially corroborated by CHAT-02, where the rider said 'Ok, coming in 2 minutes' at 09:43:44, but the driver still waited until 09:49:54, so the delay exceeded the policy threshold.
The driver's history shows 6 disputes against in the last 90 days and a 3.9 rating, which is context only and cannot establish fault or override the current-trip evidence.
The rider's strong history (5.0 rating, 900 trips, 0 disputes) is context only and cannot establish fault or override the current-trip evidence.

missingFacts: Exact rider arrival time at the pickup point, to confirm how late the rider actually was.
Whether the driver's marked arrival location matched the designated pickup pin or only the 150 m threshold.
Any rider-side GPS trace showing the rider's approach to the pickup during the wait window.

GPS-PICKUP shows a closest approach of 31 m (within the 150 m limit), a wait of 430 s from first entering the threshold until cancellation (exceeding the 300 s minimum), and CHAT-SUMMARY confirms three contact attempts (CHAT-01, CHAT-03, CALL-01) before cancellation (exceeding the minimum of one).
